**SUBJECT:** New Scheduling Policy & Rotational Model (Effective [Start Date of Next Quarter])

Our primary goal is to create a scheduling system that is **fair, predictable, and robust**, allowing us to meet our service commitments while providing you with a better work-life balance.

In alignment with direction from VP Halvard, we are moving to an **"Availability-First"** scheduling model. This new policy is designed to give you more input into your schedule, provide predictability, and ensure the hub is always staffed for success.

#### **I. Core Principles of the New Policy**

1.  **Availability-First:** Your declared availability is the primary input for building the schedule. The schedule is built *from* your availability, not assigned *to* you without input.
2.  **Predictability:** Schedules will be published for a full quarter at a time, based on a clear rotational pattern. You will know your workdays and rest days weeks in advance.
3.  **Fairness & Equity:** The system is designed to distribute weekend work and preferred days off equitably over time. All requests are handled through the same formal process.
4.  **Operational Need:** As a seven-day operation, our fundamental requirement is to have the hub fully staffed every day to meet customer demand. All scheduling is balanced against this core need.

#### **II. The Four-Team Rotational Model**

To manage our 38-person staff across a seven-day week, we will be organized into four teams (Team A, Team B, Team C, Team D). Each team will consist of 9-10 members.

These teams will work a five-day week on a rotating schedule. This ensures that everyone receives two consecutive days off each week and that weekend work is distributed evenly among all teams over a four-week cycle.

**Example Four-Week Rotational Cycle:**
(Note: This is an example pattern; the final rotation will be published with the schedule.)

*   **Week 1:** Team A has Sat/Sun off.
*   **Week 2:** Team B has Sat/Sun off.
*   **Week 3:** Team C has Sat/Sun off.
*   **Week 4:** Team D has Sat/Sun off.

During the weeks your team is not scheduled for a weekend off, your two consecutive days off will fall on weekdays (e.g., Mon/Tues, Tues/Wed, etc.). The full rotational calendar will be provided with the final schedule.

This is a four-step process that will repeat every quarter.

**Step 1: Quarterly Availability Submission (Your Input)**
Thirty (30) days before the start of a new quarter, you will receive an "Availability Declaration" form. You are required to complete and submit this form by the specified deadline. On this form, you will declare:
*   **Recurring Unavailability:** Any specific day of the week you are consistently unable to work. **This is where requests for a fixed day of rest for religious observance or other standing personal commitments must be officially submitted.** (See Note on DSP-3)
*   **Preferred Days Off:** You may rank your preferred days off.

*Note on DSP-3 (Sabbath/Day of Rest Obligation):* We are committed to accommodating requests for a recurring day of rest for religious observance where operationally feasible.
